subject: Data Engineering
title: Defense in Depth
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Defense in Depth.

hook.text: A castle doesn't rely on one wall. It has a moat, outer walls, inner walls, and a keep. Data systems need the same.

buildup.text: Defense in depth layers multiple safeguards so that no single failure causes a disaster.

discovery.text: Layers include access control, encryption, validation, monitoring, alerting, backups, and incident response.

twist.text: Every disaster in this course broke through because one layer was the only layer. Depth requires redundancy.

climax.text: No single safeguard is enough. The question is: when this one fails, what catches the problem next?

punchline.text: One wall falls. The next one holds. That's defense in depth.

quiz.question: What is the principle of defense in depth?
options: Layering multiple safeguards so no single failure causes disaster
Using the strongest possible single defense
Only defending the most valuable data
